'''George A. Scangos''' was a pharmaceutical executive and former chief executive officer of [[Vir Biotechnology]] from 2017 to 2023. Scangos was previously the chief executive officer of [[Biogen]] from 2010 to 2016 and of [[Exelixis]] from 1996 to 2010.<ref name="BioPharma Dive">{{cite news |last1=Fidler |first1=Ben |title=Veteran biotech leader George Scangos to step down as Vir CEO |url=https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/george-scangos-retire-vir-ceo-marianne-de-backer/641187/ |access-date=April 5, 2023 |work=BioPharma Dive |date=January 25, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title = George Scangos |url=https://www.bizjournals.com/sanfrancisco/stories/2007/09/24/tidbits2.html |work=www.bizjournals.com}}</ref> Prior to joining industry, Scangos was a professor of biology at [[Johns Hopkins University]].<ref name="Biogen CEO">{{cite news |title=Biogen Idec Names George Scangos Chief Executive Officer |url=https://investors.biogen.com/news-releases/news-release-details/biogen-idec-names-george-scangos-chief-executive-officer |access-date=April 5, 2023}}</ref><ref name="PharmaVoice Bio">{{cite news |last1=Ribbink |first1=Kim |title=Dr. George Scangos: Gene Excellence |url=https://www.pharmavoice.com/news/2009-04-dr-george-scangos-gene-excellence/614449/ |access-date=6 April 2023 |work=PharmaVoice |date=25 March 2009}}</ref>

==Education==
He has a BA in [[biology]] from [[Cornell University]] in 1991. He worked briefly as a lab technician at MIT and then became a sales rep for a lab supply company. Trying to get into a graduate school, he drove out to [[University of Massachusetts]] and despite never taking a microbiology course, ended up with a PhD in [[microbiology]] from the [[University of Massachusetts]] with Albey Reiner in 1977.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Scangos |first1=Georg A. |last2=Reiner |first2=Albey Mahesh |title=A unique pattern of toxic synthesis in pentitol catabolism: Implications for evolution |journal=Journal of Molecular Evolution |date=March 1, 1979 |volume=12 |issue=3 |pages=189–195 |doi=10.1007/BF01732338|pmid=374747 |bibcode=1979JMolE..12..189S |s2cid=34473235 }}</ref> He then did his postdoctoral fellowship with [[Frank Ruddle]] at [[Yale University]] where they created the first [[Genetically modified mouse|transgenic mouse]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Gordon |first1=J W |last2=Scangos |first2=G A |last3=Plotkin |first3=D J |last4=Barbosa |first4=J A |last5=Ruddle |first5=F H |title=Genetic transformation of mouse embryos by microinjection of purified DNA. |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences |date=December 1980 |volume=77 |issue=12 |pages=7380–7384 |doi=10.1073/pnas.77.12.7380|doi-access=free |pmid=6261253 |pmc=350507 |bibcode=1980PNAS...77.7380G }}</ref>

== Career ==
He was a professor of biology at Johns Hopkins University for six years before taking a sabbatical to join Molecular Diagnostics which was co-founded by Ruddle. Molecular Diagnostics and Molecular Therapeutics were acquired by [[Bayer]] and he was recruited to [[Bayer]] Biotechnology to expand their labs in 1989. With Bayer, he would lead the development of [[Factor VIII (medication)]] at the [[Berkeley, California]] campus<ref name="Biogen CEO" /><ref name="Xcomony Bio" /><ref name="PharmaVoice Bio" />

In 1996, Scangos joined Exelixis and took the company public and was responsible for building its cancer pipeline and setting up multiple partnerships. Exelixix would move to California and move into small molecule discovery and development.<ref name="PharmaVoice Bio" /> He was named CEO of Biogen Idec during the strategic battle with [[Carl Icahn]] and made a number of major changes in the direction of the company including closing down the San Diego site, moving headquarters back to Cambridge and dropping the old Idec name. This also including the pivot from oncology research to risky pipeline projects in neurology and hematology including the development of drugs for multiple sclerosis and Alzheimer's like [[aducanumab]].<ref name="Xconomy Biogen Retirement">{{cite news |last1=Fidler |first1=Ben |title=With Biogen at a Crossroads, CEO Scangos to Step Down {{!}} Xconomy |url=http://www.xconomy.com/boston/2016/07/21/with-biogen-at-a-crossroads-ceo-scangos-to-step-down/ |access-date=6 April 2023 |work=Xconomy Boston |date=21 July 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170202162449/http://www.xconomy.com/boston/2016/07/21/with-biogen-at-a-crossroads-ceo-scangos-to-step-down/ |archive-date=February 2, 2017 |language=en}}</ref><ref name="Xcomony Bio">{{cite news |last1=Timmerman |first1=Luke |title=George Scangos, the Boy From Working Class Boston, on His Road Back to Lead Biogen Idec |url=http://www.xconomy.com/boston/2011/08/31/george-scangos-the-boy-from-working-class-boston-on-his-road-back-to-lead-biogen-idec/ |access-date=6 April 2023 |work=Xconomy Boston |date=31 August 2011 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Mitchell |first1=Peter |title=Biogen Idec restructures, sharpens neurology focus |journal=Nature Biotechnology |date=1 January 2011 |volume=29 |issue=1 |pages=7–8 |doi=10.1038/nbt0111-7 |pmid=21221080|s2cid=205264959 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Timmerman |first1=Luke |title=Biogen Idec CEO on Move Back to Cambridge: "We're Working on It" |url=https://xconomy.com/boston/2011/06/16/biogen-idec-ceo-on-move-back-to-cambridge-were-working-on-it/ |access-date=6 April 2023 |work=Xconomy Boston |date=16 June 2011 |language=en}}</ref> Scangos was named CEO during the launch of Vir. He would serve as the chair of [[PhRMA]] in 2016 and was the lead of the [[Biotechnology Innovation Organization]]'s response to COVID-19.<ref>{{cite news |title=Vir Biotechnology Announces Retirement of CEO George Scangos, Ph.D.; Appoints Marianne De Backer, MSc, Ph.D., MBA, as Successor |url=https://www.biospace.com/vir-biotechnology-announces-retirement-of-ceo-george-scangos-ph-d-appoints-marianne-de-backer-msc-ph-d-mba-as-successor |work=BioSpace |date=25 January 2023}}</ref><ref name="Greek Reporter" /><ref name="STAT retirement">{{cite news |last1=Mast |first1=Jason |title=Vir CEO George Scangos to retire, after pandemic success |url=https://www.statnews.com/2023/01/25/vir-ceo-george-scangos-to-retire-after-pandemic-success/ |work=STAT |date=25 January 2023}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Scangos grew up in [[Lynn, Massachusetts]] and is of Greek descent. His father was an accountant at Exxon. His grandparents came to the US from Greece.<ref name="Greek Reporter">{{cite news |last1=Kampouris |first1=Nick |title=Greek-American Scientist Heads Global Campaign for Coronavirus Treatment |url=https://greekreporter.com/2020/03/09/exclusive-greek-american-scientist-heads-global-campaign-for-coronavirus-treatment/ |access-date=April 5, 2023 |publisher=Greek Reporter |date=March 9, 2020}}</ref>
